title: Israel Launches Strikes Across Southern Lebanon as Katz Vows to 'Settle Scores'
excerpt: Defense Minister Israel Katz pledged forceful retaliation after a Hezbollah drone attack seriously wounded three IDF soldiers near Nabatieh.
body:
• Israeli forces launched heavy strikes around the Ali Taher Ridge near Nabatieh in southern Lebanon overnight, following a Hezbollah explosive-drone attack that seriously wounded three IDF soldiers.
  • Defense Minister Israel Katz declared that "no account on any front will remain unsettled," signaling continued Israeli military aggression despite the June ceasefire.
  • The IDF confirmed killing a second senior Hezbollah commander amid the latest exchange, as fighting persists nearly two months after the US-brokered security agreement.
  • Over 4,330 Lebanese have been killed since the war began on March 2, with the ceasefire largely failing to halt violence in southern Lebanon.

Israeli forces launched a wave of strikes across southern Lebanon overnight on Sunday, targeting positions around the strategic Ali Taher Ridge near Nabatieh, according to Lebanese and Israeli media reports. The attacks came a day after three IDF soldiers were seriously wounded by a Hezbollah explosive-drone attack in the region.

Katz's Vow of Retaliation

Defense Minister Israel Katz responded to the drone attack with a combative pledge on social media platform X. "No account on any front will remain unsettled," he wrote. "We will forcefully defend our soldiers and citizens."

https://x.com/TheCradleMedia/status/2088914064663581079

"No account on any front will remain unsettled. We will forcefully defend our soldiers and citizens."

— Israel Katz, Israeli Defense Minister, on X

The statement underscored Israel's refusal to de-escalate in Lebanon despite the June 19 ceasefire agreement brokered by the United States. Israeli officials have repeatedly said their forces will remain in a self-declared security zone extending roughly 10 kilometers into southern Lebanon for as long as necessary to protect northern Israeli communities from Hezbollah attacks.

Ceasefire in Name Only

The June ceasefire, followed by a US-brokered security arrangement on June 26, was meant to ease hostilities along the Israel-Lebanon border. Under the deal, Israel would gradually withdraw from designated "pilot zones" as the Lebanese army assumes responsibility for security. But in practice, the fighting has barely slowed.

Israel has continued airstrikes, ground operations, and building demolitions across the buffer zone, while Hezbollah has employed cheap kamikaze drones and anti-tank missiles that have killed and wounded Israeli soldiers. The IDF said it had killed a second senior Hezbollah commander in the latest round of fighting, though it did not immediately release his name.

Since the war began on March 2, 2026 — when Hezbollah fired on Israel in solidarity with Iran following the outbreak of the broader US-Israeli war with Tehran — over 4,330 Lebanese have been killed and more than one million displaced. At least 32 Israeli soldiers and four civilians have been killed by Hezbollah in the same period.

Escalation Despite Diplomacy

The latest violence follows a pattern of escalation that has undermined every diplomatic effort. On August 5, two Israeli reservists were killed and four critically injured by an IED in Majdal Zoun, prompting the IDF to order the evacuation of al-Mansouri and carry out "precision strikes" in the area. The 401st Brigade announced on August 2 that it had destroyed 1,200 Hezbollah tunnels during its eight-month deployment.

Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem rejected the Lebanese cabinet's August 7 vote to disarm the group, calling it "unacceptable" — a stance that Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam condemned as a threat of civil war. US envoy Tom Barrack urged Israel to match Lebanon's steps toward implementation, but Israel has shown no signs of withdrawing.

What It Means for the Region

The continued fighting in southern Lebanon threatens to destabilize an already fragile region. For India, which maintains diplomatic ties with both Israel and Lebanon and has hundreds of thousands of nationals working across the Middle East, the prolonged conflict raises concerns about regional stability and energy supply chains. India has called for restraint from all parties and supported diplomatic solutions.

What's Next

With Israel's October elections approaching and Netanyahu under domestic pressure, analysts expect the military posture in Lebanon to harden rather than soften. The disarmament impasse between Lebanon's government and Hezbollah makes a full Israeli withdrawal unlikely in the near term, keeping southern Lebanon locked in a cycle of violence.
